subject.title: fix(agents): avoid symlink-follow in auth.json bootstrap

question: Should OpenClaw retain the exact-mode and no-final-path-chmod behavior in its shared replacement wrapper, or should `@openclaw/fs-safe` own that invariant before this PR merges?
rationale: The patch appears correct and well proven, but it changes a plugin-facing security primitive used beyond auth storage; source review cannot safely choose the permanent dependency ownership boundary or intended cross-platform guarantee.

options.title: Keep the OpenClaw wrapper
options.body: Land the proven wrapper after secops and fs-safe owner approval, then track any upstream consolidation separately.

options.title: Move the invariant upstream first
options.body: Implement and release the secure replacement behavior in `@openclaw/fs-safe`, then reduce OpenClaw back to a thin export.

options.title: Narrow this PR to bootstrap
options.body: Land only the `auth.json` bootstrap repair and track the shared post-rename chmod race in a separate owner-reviewed item.

recommendation.title: Keep the OpenClaw wrapper
recommendation.body: Land the proven wrapper after secops and fs-safe owner approval, then track any upstream consolidation separately.

likelyOwner.reason: He is a published `@openclaw/fs-safe` maintainer and the strongest available routing candidate for coordinating the dependency-boundary decision with OpenClaw secops.
